==English==

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂eym-}}
{{bor+|en|la|imitātus}}, {{glossary|perfect}} {{glossary|active}} {{glossary|participle}} of {{m|la|imitor||to copy, portray, imitate}}, see {{af|en|-ate|id1=verb|pos1=verb-forming suffix}}. Cognate with {{cog|fr|imiter}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɪmɪteɪt/|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-imitate.ogg|a=US}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# To [[follow]] as a [[model]] or a [[pattern]]; to make a [[copy]], [[counterpart]] or [[semblance]] of.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1870|author=Shirley Hibberd|title=Rustic Adornments for Homes of Taste|page=170
|passage=Another bird quickly learned to '''imitate''' the song of a canary that was mated with it, but as the parrakeet improved in the performance the canary degenerated, and came at last to mingle the other bird's harsh chitterings with its own proper music.}}
#* {{RQ:en:New York Times|date=2007-02-20|author=Tina Kelley|title=A Wet Wind Tunnel So Ships Can Move Faster and Better|url=http://www.nytimes.com/2007/02/20/nyregion/20ink.html
|passage=A wave simulator in the tank can re-enact tsunamis and northeasters, and '''imitate''' wave conditions from midocean.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20221218224425/https://www.nytimes.com/2007/02/20/nyregion/20ink.html}}
#* {{RQ:Time|title=Inside the Race to Build the World's First Commercial Octopus Farm|author=Tik Root|date=August 21 2019|passage=The room was dark and cool, lit with a dim red light. “This was designed to '''imitate''' a cave,” said Rosas.|url=https://time.com/5657927/farm-raised-octopus/|accessdate=2 April 2020|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190828122535/https://time.com/5657927/farm-raised-octopus/|archivedate=28 August 2019}}

====Synonyms====
* See also [[Thesaurus:imitate]]
